spec.idea: Each simdgroup computes 4 output rows, with each lane handling one packed uint32 (8 weights) per step. Dequantization is factored as scale*Σ(x·q) + bias*Σx, so the bias term costs one multiply per group, and each lane's x loads are reused across all 4 rows.

spec.header:
template<typename P>
inline uint2 ld2(P p) { return uint2(p[0], p[1]); }
spec.idea: Each lane loads 16 weights per row as one 8-byte uint2 and uses masked nibbles against x pre-scaled by 16^-i, which removes the per-element shifts. This halves the loop trips and the scale/bias loads, and x and the group sum are still shared across 4 rows.

spec.header:
template<typename P>
inline uint4 ld4(P p) { return uint4(p[0], p[1], p[2], p[3]); }
spec.idea: Each lane loads 32 weights per row as one 16-byte uint4 for 4 rows, all loads issued before any math, so there are half as many loop trips and more bytes in flight per lane than k001; masked nibbles against 16^-i pre-scaled x still avoid shifts.

spec.header:
template<typename P>
inline uint2 ld2(P p) { return uint2(p[0], p[1]); }
spec.idea: k001's 16-weights-per-lane masked-nibble kernel with the next iteration's weight/scale/bias loads software-pipelined ahead of the current math to keep more bytes in flight.
